blockers.quote: About 128 trillion dollars (c09). You have more than that. In cents.
blockers.why: Claim c09 supports world GDP at about $128 trillion. On day fifty-five, 2^54 cents equals approximately €180 trillion (as noted in c09 and shown on the tag in line 240: 180.143.985.094.819,84). Stating 'You have more than that. In cents.' is an arithmetic slip and contradicts the claim: 128 trillion cents is only $1.28 trillion, which fails to pass world GDP. The balance surpasses world GDP in euros, not cents.
blockers.fix: About 128 trillion dollars (c09). You have more than that. In euros.

blockers.quote: In 1324, Mansa Musa came through Cairo and gave away so much gold that gold there stayed cheap for at least twelve years (c06).
blockers.why: Claim c06's verbatim quote ('Musa's gift-giving caused a depreciation in the value of gold in Egypt.' ... 'it dropped to less than 22 dirhams afterward and did not go above that number for at least twelve years.') supports that Musa's gift-giving depreciated gold in Egypt for at least twelve years, but does not support the spoken date '1324' or the narrower geographic scope 'Cairo'. The year 1324 needs a source in the quote, and Cairo overstates the verbatim quote's scope ('in Egypt').
blockers.fix: Mansa Musa came through Egypt and gave away so much gold that gold there stayed cheap for at least twelve years (c06). (date 1324 needs a source)

blockers.why: Claim c04's verbatim quote ('While wages, salaries, pensions and rents were automatically converted at a rate of 1:1' ... 'children up to the age of 14 could exchange 2,000 GDR marks 1:1,' 'adults up to the age of 59 4,000 GDR marks and senior citizens up to 6,000 GDR marks.' 'All higher sums were converted at a rate of 2:1.') supports the conversion rates, but the quote itself contains no date. The spoken date 'first of July, 1990' needs a source in the verbatim quote.
blockers.fix: The night the currencies switched (c04). (date 1 July 1990 needs a source in the verbatim quote)
